title: *Climate Risk Profile Somalia*
organization: Weathering Risk / Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK)
methodology: AGRICA methodology; multi-model RCP2.6/RCP6.0 projections plus sector synthesis
limitations: Socioeconomic change not included in climate models; precipitation, river flooding, crop and ecosystem projections have substantial uncertainty; not a current humanitarian assessment.

title: *Somalia's Third Generation Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0)*
organization: Somalia; reproduced by FAO/FAOLEX through InforMEA
limitations: Policy intent, not evaluated implementation; accessible page is a UN/FAOLEX reproduction rather than the official UNFCCC PDF. (InforMEA)

title: *National Adaptation Plan - Somalia*
limitations: Publication page verified; full 26 MB document timed out in this browsing environment, so internal NAP locators are LOCATOR NOT VERIFIED and no substantive evidence record below depends on them. (UNFCCC)

title: *Climate-related security risks and peacebuilding in Somalia*
methodology: Single-case plausibility probe; qualitative process tracing; literature plus 27 interviews and expert consultations
limitations: Older; UNSOM-focused; explicitly limited in generalizability and does not establish a national causal coefficient. (SIPRI)

title: *Environmental Peacemaking in Somalia: Integrated Climate and Conflict Analysis of the Newly Liberated Areas of Hirshabelle and Galmudug*
geographic_coverage: Newly Liberated Areas, Hirshabelle and Galmudug
methodology: Literature/regulatory review, expert consultations and Mogadishu stakeholder workshop
limitations: Localized case; consultation/synthesis evidence rather than causal identification; must not be generalized nationally.

title: *SWALIM Quarterly Newsletter: Jan-March 2026*
organization: FAO Somalia Water and Land Information Management
methodology: Combined Drought Index, hydrometeorological monitoring, satellite/DEM analysis, field observers and community feedback
limitations: Operational quarterly monitoring, not climate attribution or long-term projection.

title: *FAO GIEWS Country Brief: Somalia*
geographic_coverage: National with market and livelihood-zone examples
methodology: Cereal balance, food-price monitoring, Earth observation and IPC evidence
limitations: Snapshot; national totals coexist with geographically specific examples; does not independently identify causal conflict effects. (FAOHome)

title: *Somalia IPC Acute Food Insecurity and Acute Malnutrition Analysis - Updated Projection April-June 2026*
organization: Somalia IPC Technical Working Group / IPC partners
methodology: IPC protocols; government, FAO/FSNAU, WFP, UNICEF, WHO, FEWS NET, REACH and cluster inputs
limitations: Projection conditional on evolving rainfall, prices, assistance and conflict; some areas have scarce evidence due to limited/no humanitarian access.

title: *UNHCR Somalia PSMN 2026 Q2 Report*
limitations: Web publication page gives high-level result but limited methodology detail; percentage refers to recorded displacement, not population-wide causal attribution. (UNHCR Data Portal)

title: *Support for Strengthening Climate Change Adaptation Planning for the Federal Republic of Somalia*
methodology: Programme diagnostics, institutional reviews and reported outputs
limitations: Mostly programme theory/output reporting; page still says “Under Implementation” despite listed 2020-24 dates; effectiveness not independently evaluated here. (UNDP Climate Change Adaptation)

title: *The World Bank Group in the Federal Republic of Somalia, Fiscal Years 2013-23: Country Program Evaluation*
methodology: Project evidence, secondary datasets, literature review, 43 evaluative reports from 18 partners and interviews
limitations: Evaluates World Bank Group engagement rather than the full Somali institutional/humanitarian system; some outcome evidence originates in project reporting.

title: *Evaluation of Somalia WFP Country Strategic Plan 2022-2025*
limitations: WFP-specific; effectiveness attribution occurs in a highly dynamic multi-actor crisis; resilience and capacity-strengthening results constrained by funding/logistics. (World Food Programme)

title: *Joint Communiqué - Activation of the National Preparedness Plan for Food and Nutrition Security Crises*
organization: Federal Government of Somalia and partners / World Bank host
limitations: Evidence of activation, coordination and intended mechanisms - not evidence that the plan subsequently reduced losses. (World Bank)

title: *UNDP Somalia Annual Report 2025*
limitations: Self-reported outputs/results; no counterfactual; reported peacebuilding and resilience achievements should not be interpreted as independently demonstrated causal effects. (UNDP)
